verdict.rationale: The evidence shows no built-in AI assistant. Anytype instead exposes notes to external AI tools: an official MCP server lets assistants work with the Anytype API in natural language, and an agents skill gives Claude Code, Cursor and similar tools a 'safe way to read, search, and modify Objects', all through a local API that runs entirely on localhost and offline. That makes grounded Q&A and drafting possible only with third-party tools, and data controls rest on the localhost architecture rather than on documented AI-specific scoping. Missing for 10: a native in-app assistant, documented summarize/draft/Q&A features, granular controls over which spaces or objects the AI can see, and independent hands-on corroboration.
